solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some pieces of music played in hall (eg Rossini)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these three clue words

explanation.surface: A concert-goer notes that a few movements by Rossini were performed in a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' is a link word joining the definition to the hidden word; the brackets are only there for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast movements of a symphony or sonata are each marked with this Italian tempo, so the plural names pieces of music.

clue.text: Like featuring revolting Bild off- the-cuff comments?

indicators.note: something featuring another holds it within, so the two letters for 'like' wrap the next piece

parts.note: like means as, as in 'do like I do'

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the word Bild is read backwards

explanation.surface: A question about whether the German tabloid Bild's comments are unscripted, with Bild described as revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: Bild is a German tabloid newspaper; 'revolting' is the reversal signal, not a judgement on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised remarks made without preparation are spoken spontaneously, which is exactly what this phrase describes.

clue.text: Baez's only weakness? She has a terrible work ethic

definitions.text: She has a terrible work ethic

indicators.note: a weakness here is the fodder being unsound, so the letters of the two clue words collapse and are rearranged

explanation.surface: The folk singer Joan Baez's one flaw, it seems, is that she is idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weakness' signals that the nine letters of BAEZS ONLY are shuffled; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal name for an idle person, someone with no appetite for work.

clue.text: Regaining my mood, playing a classic song

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are toyed with and set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recovers their good spirits by putting on an old favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the fifteen letters of REGAINING MY MOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1930 Hoagy Carmichael number, famously recorded by Ray Charles, is a standard of American popular music.

clue.text: Loire city lists other ranks first

indicators.note: first says the soldiers' abbreviation goes at the front, ahead of the word for lists

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A city on the Loire draws up its rolls, putting enlisted soldiers at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a noun but is the verb: to list is to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The city where Joan of Arc lifted the siege lies on the Loire in central France.

clue.text: Insignificant individual, quiet, terribly prim

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word prim is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of a meek, silent, dreadfully prudish nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny crustacean gives its name, informally, to a small or unimportant person.

clue.text: A gifted songwriter? Yeah, magic choral works

indicators.note: works here means is worked over, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan enthuses that a talented writer's choral pieces are magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun for compositions but signals the anagram of YEAH MAGIC CHORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The American composer of Stardust and Georgia on My Mind is one of the most celebrated popular songwriters.

clue.text: Independent area hosting small business somewhere in the Balearics

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest inside, so the two letters wrap the next piece

parts.note: biz is a short, informal word for business

explanation.surface: A self-governing region on one of the Spanish islands is home to a little firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' puts BIZ between the I and the A.
explanation.definitionFit: This party island is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, alongside Majorca and Minorca.

clue.text: Quiet knight, tense, suppressing rising anger with child

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word anger is reversed

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A calm, tense knight keeps a lid on his mounting fury in the company of a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads upwards, and 'suppressing' puts the reversed anger on top of the knight and tense letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with child is an old-fashioned way of saying expecting a baby.

clue.text: Defined as "tall, blond, blue-eyed" in lexicon (or dictionary)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters running across these clue words

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry that defines a word as tall, blond and blue-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defined as' is a link word; the letters run from the end of 'lexicon' into 'dictionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stereotype of Scandinavian people is tall, fair-haired and blue-eyed, which this adjective describes.

clue.text: Roman squad left Italian WWII battle, having lost an indefinite number

indicators.note: having lost means a piece is dropped from the battle's name

parts.note: Anzio was the site of the Allied landings and battle in Italy in 1944
N is the mathematician's symbol for an indefinite number

explanation.surface: A Roman military unit withdraws from a Second World War battle after heavy losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman squad' sounds like a legion but means a football team; 'having lost' drops the N from the battle's name.
explanation.definitionFit: SS Lazio is one of the two big football clubs based in Rome, so it is a Roman team.

clue.text: Being 50, ace leader of musical gang retired, Eisenhower's dead ringer

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the ace letter and the bandleader's name are read backwards

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
Kool led the funk band Kool and the Gang
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old retired bandleader turns out to be Eisenhower's double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns A + KOOL into LOOKA; 'Being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is someone who resembles another person exactly, a double.

clue.text: Piano group covering Deck of Cards singer, mostly

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the group's letters go around the singer

parts.note: a band is a musical group

indicators.note: mostly means most of the name is kept and its end is dropped

parts.note: Max Bygraves, a British entertainer, had a hit with the spoken song Deck of Cards in 1973

explanation.surface: A band covers an old song and lets its piano carry the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' here drops the last three letters of the singer's surname, and 'covering' wraps the group round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A small horizontal grand piano is a type of piano, so the general word defines it.

clue.text: Long period of time before noon

indicators.note: before puts the period of time ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is a long while until midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective attached to 'period' but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or pine for it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Gran is going out looking dishevelled

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters break out of their place and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grandma is heading out the door looking scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' rearranges GRAN IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing tattered old clothes looks shabby and unkempt.

clue.text: Mortification of Greek placed in restraint

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the Greek letters go within the restraint

parts.note: a chain is a restraint

explanation.surface: A Greek prisoner is humiliated at being put in shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means vexation or embarrassment at a humiliation, much like mortification.

clue.text: A floating asset moving between banks

definitions.text: A floating asset moving between banks

parts.words: A floating asset moving between banks
parts.note: sounds like money circulating among financial banks, but means a vessel travelling between river banks

explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests finance and 'floating asset' suggests money; it is a boat that floats between riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer on the Mississippi is a vessel that travels up and down between a river's two shores.

clue.text: Begin to comprehend taking drugs regularly — it's magical!

indicators.note: to comprehend means to take in, so the word for begin holds the next piece

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of drugs is taken

explanation.surface: Someone starts to understand things by taking drugs, and finds it magical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the odd letters of drugs, and 'to comprehend' holds them inside the word for begin; 'taking' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparkle in fairy tales is the stuff of magic, and the word is also a Hoagy Carmichael song.

clue.text: Sit back, taking in old-fashioned healthy infusions

indicators.note: taking in means holding within, so the reversed word wraps the next piece
back means the word sit is read backwards

parts.note: sane once meant healthy in body, a sense now archaic

explanation.surface: Relax and drink some quaint, wholesome herbal teas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' marks the old bodily sense of the word for healthy; 'back' and 'taking in' wrap the reversed sit round it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are herbal teas, made by steeping leaves or flowers in hot water.

clue.text: Salt water, lad?

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt water' reads as one phrase, but 'Salt' is the verb definition and 'water' alone gives SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt food is to flavour it, which is what the verb meaning add spice or salt means.

clue.text: Substitute always running back, tackling Salah

indicators.note: tackling means grappling around, so the reversed word wraps the footballer's letters
running back means the word for always reads backwards

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
Mo Salah is the Egyptian footballer who plays for Liverpool

explanation.surface: A football report: a substitute, forever charging backwards, tackles the striker Mohamed Salah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' looks like a noun but is the verb, as a manager takes a player off; 'running back' and 'tackling' sound like football too.
explanation.definitionFit: To substitute a player is to take him off the pitch, as a manager does when making a change.

clue.text: Famous Egyptian recipe's beginning with ground sesame

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its first letter, here of recipe
ground means crushed, so the letters of sesame are pounded into a new order

explanation.surface: A cookbook tip: a well-known Egyptian dish starts with crushed sesame seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the anagram signal, not a kitchen step; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Several pharaohs bore this name, most famously Rameses II, so it is a famous ancient Egyptian.

clue.text: Old machine gun emplacement above Dutch North Sea port

indicators.note: above, in a down clue, puts the gun ahead of the Dutch letter

parts.note: the Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War, set in place here

explanation.surface: An old gun post overlooks a Dutch port on the North Sea coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten gun is the British submachine gun of the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: This Belgian coastal town is a ferry and fishing port on the North Sea.

clue.text: Posh crackers for a yen?

parts.note: Ritz is a well-known brand of crackers
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A query whether someone is mad about a craving for something fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like an adjective meaning mad, but it is the biscuit brand; 'for a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective, from the Ritz hotels, means luxurious, glamorous and expensive.

clue.text: Find time to compete

parts.note: to race is to compete

explanation.surface: A detective urges finding the time to race against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something lost is to track it down, the verb sense of tracing.

clue.text: Military body to give guns to Young Conservative men: an afterthought

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
YC is the abbreviation for a Young Conservative, a member of the UK Conservative Party's youth wing
OR (other ranks) is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, the men
PS (postscript) is a note added to a letter as an afterthought

explanation.surface: As a late thought, someone suggests issuing weapons to young Tory men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' gives OR, the other ranks of the army.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large army formation of two or more divisions, a military unit.

clue.text: First off: Uncle Sam union to be wound up, everyone agreed

indicators.note: first off means the first letter is taken off the front of uncle
to be wound up means to be twisted round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: First item of business: an American union is to be dissolved, by common consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' gives U from Uncle, and 'to be wound up' rearranges SAM UNION to NANIMOUS. 'wound up' looks like closing a business down.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote in which all are of one mind is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Love three musical notes

parts.note: A is a note of the scale, a letter name for one pitch
do (or doh) is the first note of the sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of a little three-note phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to worship or be devoted to, a strong synonym of love.

clue.text: In Turkey, final destination unknown

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
the end is where a journey finishes
Y is an algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: A traveller in Turkey has no idea where the trip will finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition but is the definition, as in 'the in thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is fashionable, so the short word is a synonym of fashionable.

clue.text: One dead and buried in the ground alone

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: buried in means put inside, so the word for dead goes within the earth

parts.note: sod is turf, the ground
the late someone is a dead person

explanation.surface: A lonely figure, dead and buried in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is cut off from others is solitary and on their own.
